verdict.rationale: Lovable documents an official MCP server that lets the user's own AI agent create projects, send messages to Lovable, inspect code, and deploy apps. This means an external agent can drive the builder alongside the built-in one. However, the evidence shows that agent working through Lovable's built-in agent, not replacing it. Git sync lets locally made edits sync back, but that is a general IDE workflow rather than a documented agent-driving capability, so it earns no credit here. Missing for 10: evidence that an external agent can directly edit project code in place of the built-in agent, details on tool scope and limits, and independent or hands-on corroboration of the MCP-server workflow.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can connect my own coding agent to the project so it drives the builder alongside or instead of the built-in one

citations.quote: your AI agent can create projects, send messages to Lovable, inspect code, deploy apps, and more, all without leaving the client you're already working in
